chains.title: Why colonial agriculture stagnated
steps: Profit from farming goes to zamindars, not cultivators
Fixed revenue dates: zamindars extract maximum rent
Little is invested to improve agriculture

chains.title: The two-fold motive and the fall of handicrafts
steps: Britain wants raw materials and a market for its goods
The demand is met by cheap British imports

chains.title: Export surplus and the drain of wealth
steps: India exports primary products, imports finished goods
It pays for the colonial office, British wars and invisible imports
No gold or silver flows in: the drain of wealth
Essentials like food grains, clothes and kerosene scarce at home

chains.title: Railways and commercialisation
steps: Farmers shift from food crops to cash crops for sale
Cash crops ultimately serve British industries
Village self-sufficiency is hurt; few farmers gain
